questions.explain: Put the distributor on cloud A near the publisher so the high-volume publisher-to-distributor leg is local; only the distributor-to-subscriber leg crosses the boundary. Never stretch the publisher-to-distributor link across clouds.
options: On cloud B near the subscriber, for balanced load
In a third cloud for neutrality
Co-located with the publisher on the same VM
On cloud A near the publisher — never stretch the publisher-to-distributor link across clouds
questions.q: Where should the distributor be placed for transactional replication across clouds?

questions.explain: Snapshot initialization across the WAN is slow and expensive (egress on every byte); instead seed the subscriber from a native backup restored on cloud B, then initialize replication from the backup.
options: Seed from a native backup restored on cloud B, then initialize replication from the backup
Take a full snapshot over the WAN — egress is negligible
Ship the snapshot on USB drives by courier
Re-create the schema by hand and bulk-copy with BCP
questions.q: What is the chapter's recommended way to initialize a cross-cloud subscriber?

questions.explain: Requirements: EC2/VMs/GCE on both sides, async mode with measured latency, and independent quorum in each site — cloud witnesses in each cloud's storage, never one witness for both sites.
options: Synchronous mode with a single cloud witness
Managed services on both sides with sync commit
Async mode, VMs on both sides, and independent quorum (a witness in each cloud)
Bidirectional writes with 'we'll coordinate writes' agreements
questions.q: What are the requirements for a distributed availability group across clouds?

questions.explain: DDL goes through the same pipeline as DML — the migration-based deployment runs on every replica in dependency order (publisher first, then subscribers). Relying on automatic DDL propagation across a cloud boundary invites a 3 AM surprise.
options: Rely on transactional replication's automatic DDL propagation
Run the migration-based deployment on every replica in dependency order (publisher first, then subscribers)
Apply schema changes only to subscribers
Freeze the schema once replication is configured
questions.q: How should schema changes be handled in a cross-cloud replication topology?

questions.explain: The sequence: stop writes on cloud A, let replication drain and verify zero lag (failing over with undelivered transactions is data loss you chose), promote on cloud B, redirect clients, verify critical transactions.
options: Fail over immediately, then check lag afterward
Promote cloud B while writes continue on cloud A
Redirect DNS first, then stop writes
Stop writes, let replication drain and verify zero lag, then promote and redirect clients
questions.q: What is the correct cross-cloud failover sequence?
